verdict.rationale: Grok Build's docs offer "Explain this repo" and per-file walkthroughs as first prompts. Its plan mode explores the codebase and drafts a plan before any edit, which directly serves finding where to start changes. AGENTS.md architecture notes further ground the agent's understanding. Missing for 10: in-depth docs on how codebase exploration or indexing works (e.g., dependency or architecture mapping), and independent hands-on corroboration of codebase-explanation quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can understand how a codebase fits together to find where to start making changes

citations.quote: Useful first prompts: Explain this repo. @src/main.rs Walk me through this file.
In plan mode the agent explores the codebase and drafts a plan for your approval before it edits anything.
Put coding conventions, build and test commands, and architecture notes in an `AGENTS.md` at your repo root, and Grok follows them without being told each session.
